inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,924 logical lines. The paper proves the leading-order maximum of log|zeta| on typical fixed-length critical-line intervals by combining a short second-moment upper bound with a much richer lower-bound chain: move slightly off the critical line, invert zeta with a finite mollifier, replace its logarithm by prime-block Dirichlet polynomials, approximate their joint laws by a coarse branching-random-walk structure, and close a second-moment argument using one- and two-point large deviations. The text layer is coherent, but many displayed formulas have extraction artifacts and require source-image verification before exact reuse.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,849 logical lines. This review develops a deliberately tentative Riemann-zero/quantum-chaos analogy by matching the explicit prime formula with a periodic-orbit trace formula, then testing that dictionary against long-orbit universality, diagonal and off-diagonal spectral statistics, Riemann-Siegel resummation, and a candidate XP Hamiltonian. Its strongest semantic value lies in the representation bridge and in its explicit failure conditions: random-matrix universality is nonuniform, off-diagonal correlations are indispensable, the quantum Riemann-Siegel analogue is costly, and XP remains unbounded with no effective self-adjoint boundary condition. Displayed formulas are broadly readable but source-image checks are required for exact constants and normalizations.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,112 logical lines. The paper defines a fractional derivative of zeta through log-power Dirichlet coefficients, replaces a complex Caputo operator by the forward Grunwald-Letnikov operator to obtain a generalized Leibniz rule, simplifies an unwieldy fractional functional equation, derives a quasisymmetric completed form, and relates the derivative to eta and to a prime series on a restricted left-half-plane strip. The source itself emphasizes that fractional differentiation is nonunique, zero localization remains out of reach, and the prime result is only convergence/divergence equivalence. The text is readable, but every exact infinite-series identity and complex phase should be checked against the PDF.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 756 logical lines. The paper diagnoses why long-Dirichlet-polynomial methods cease to reproduce high zeta moments by studying the second and fourth shifted moments in two directions. Descending from the moment recipe organizes terms by swap count and shows when each appears as polynomial length crosses T and T^2; ascending from divisor coefficients recovers the diagonal and Type-I off-diagonals but has no mechanism for the two-swap contribution. An exact Fourier/Mellin identity makes the second moment work, whereas the fourth-moment descent additionally assumes an unproved uniform shifted formula. The source ends by identifying the missing correlation family rather than claiming the problem solved.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 310 logical lines. This announcement proves the ternary Goldbach statement conditionally on GRH by composing three independently bounded components: a circle-method asymptotic above 10^20, an explicit GRH prime-gap lemma reducing every smaller odd n to an even remainder below 1.615 times 10^12, and a computationally certified binary Goldbach range extending beyond that remainder. The computational section improves the verification representation from regenerating all primes in each large interval to precomputing small-prime bitsets and shifting them by a short list of primes near the interval base. OCR degrades several inequalities and symbols, so numerical constants and exact formulas require scan verification, but the proof architecture is recoverable from prose.
